public_rationale: Primary studies establish that diffusion models can memorize and reproduce training images. Controlled experiments also show that caption conditioning affects copying. This supports part of Marcus's account, but the retrieved evidence does not establish that the absence of an originality assessor explains the copying. Scoring the complete causal claim as supported would go beyond these findings.
limitations: The evidence concerns particular diffusion models and experimental settings.
Copying, memorization, originality, and legal plagiarism are not interchangeable.
The studies identify contributing factors rather than a complete explanation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Near-plagiarism results from generative systems reconstructing data fragments in statistically probable ways without any mechanism to assess originality.

statement.excerpt: Near-plagiarism comes from reconstructing those bits in statistically probable ways, without having a mechanism like an originality-assessor to investigate the novelty of the reconstruction.

our_interpretation: Near-plagiarism means substantial reproduction of identifiable training material; this is not a legal determination.
Read reconstructing bits as statistical generation from learned representations, rather than necessarily assembling literal stored fragments.
The complete claim combines a proposed copying mechanism with the absence of originality assessment.
Demonstrating memorization or copying supports part of the explanation but does not establish the causal role of missing originality checks.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled studies connect statistical generation to substantial training-material reproduction and establish that absent originality assessment materially explains the resulting copying.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled studies reject the proposed generation mechanism or its claimed relationship to originality assessment. Evidence that some systems contain checks contradicts only a universal absence-of-checks reading.

evidence.explanation: The extraction results support the component that generation can reproduce learned training material. They do not establish that missing originality assessment caused the copying.

Controlled experiments identify caption conditioning and training-data properties as influences on copying, and test mitigations that change conditioning. They qualify the broad explanation but do not isolate the effect of an originality assessor.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled comparisons that independently vary originality assessment and the proposed reconstruction mechanism, using a defined threshold for substantial reproduction.
